environmentNotes: Host Docker address pools were exhausted by other projects. The walkthrough pre-created each project's two Compose networks with explicit 10.239.30-35.x/24 subnets and the Compose project/network labels. The Compose files, services and network names stay as the articles define them.

An owned Mailpit (openlaw-docs-41255c61-lc-mail, alias lc-mail) was the controlled relay recipient on every project network. An owned MinIO (alias lc-minio) served the S3 storage fault. Both are removed.
Production authentication rate limits stayed on. Sign-ins that got HTTP 429 were retried after a pause.
Docker Compose 5.5.1 labels each built image with its project name, so the same source builds to a different image ID in each project. The build steps came from the build cache.

Installation directories were fresh git clones of https://github.com/juggernog20/OpenLaw.git under ~/.cache/openlaw-docs-lc. Keys, fixture passwords and backups stayed there and were deleted at teardown.

failedStepDispositions.disposition: The script did not wait out the production sign-in rate limit (HTTP 429). That first fixture was destroyed with its own project (down -v) and rebuilt from the same baseline; the rerun passed. Not an article observation.
The browser helper read /api/v1/me before the session existed. The helper now polls the session; the rerun at 15:24 passed on the same upgraded instance.

The starting build d1d098ba web client showed 'Something went wrong. The page could not load.' at /login in headless Chromium with no failed request. The recovery target was then checked through the same origin with the HTTP sign-in API (recorded as recovery-verify). The candidate web client works; the upgrade article does not depend on the older client.

recreate() was declared async and its result was read as a plain object. The helper was fixed and all four steps were rerun and passed from 15:31. The interrupted run left the retained key in place and had already re-extracted the file archive.

Confirmed twice (diag-startup and this recheck, plus one manual run). After a failed bind, docker compose ps --all lists app and worker in state 'created'; they are not removed. docker compose ps without --all does not list them. The article's port row says the failed bind 'leaves the app and worker containers removed'. The recovery it gives (correct the port, start the containers again) worked.
The DocuSign card must be opened before the Signing updates control appears. Rerun passed.

observations: Upgrade start: the worker exited once with 'the worker could not start the job queue' (a query on auto_doc_generations) about 0.4 s after the app logged the reconcile line, and the restart policy started it 2 s later. The upgrade article already tells the operator to read docker compose logs --tail=100 app worker and wait for readiness; nothing needed an action.

Upgrade: the Contributor became a Business User through migration 0109. Its staff API reach changed from 200 to 403, and its portal reach matched its baseline reach exactly (member Contract 200, other and Confidential Contracts 404).

App keeps restarting row: with an unresolvable DATABASE_URL host, the first app error on this host was 'Connection terminated due to connection timeout', not getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND. The daemon uses a fixed DNS server. The article names no specific message.
AI analysis Settings: the Test connection button was not found on an unconfigured AI analysis page. Not needed for any claimed result; provider diagnostics stay blocked under C42/C43.

operator-troubleshooting.reason: Port row: a failed bind leaves app and worker in state 'created', not removed (doc-error). Every other induced fault matched the article.
